chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from his brother Al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Yaqteen, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the man who hires a ship for a year, or less, or more. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The hire charge is binding until the time for which it was hired, and the choice in taking the hire charge belongs to its owner; if he wishes, he takes it, and if he wishes, he leaves it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the hire charge (kirā) for a rented ship or house in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the contractual stability of *ijārah* (leasing), affirming that the lessee’s obligation to pay remains fixed for the agreed term, while the lessor retains the unilateral right (*khiyār*) to accept or waive the fee. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on the lessor’s prerogative in commercial agreements, distinguishing between the fixed duration of the contract and the discretionary nature of the compensation. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Islamic commercial law regarding the enforcement of rental dues.
